question: When a ticket rests on a stale or false premise about this codebase, does an investigator using only Qodo Codebase Wisdom's read tools catch it?

tickets.title: Only the dependency line of Depends on counts
truePremises: writtenDependencies() in packages/harness/src/ticket-ready.ts reads the Depends on section and matches #N with a regex
ticket sections come from factory.json through loadFactory() in packages/harness/src/factory-config.ts
packages/harness/src/ticket-ready.test.ts has a test named 'reads blockers written in Depends on'

tickets.title: Prove the unit project never runs an integration test
tickets.plantedPremise: A root-level vitest.config.test.ts exists and already asserts both project names
tickets.reality: No such file exists at d9cbe5f; vitest.config.ts has no test next to it. The file was deleted in 1f247d1 (10 Nov), when the test it held moved into factory-tick.test.ts.
truePremises: vitest.config.ts defines two projects named unit and integration
npm test runs 'vitest run --project unit' and npm run test:integration runs the integration project

tickets.title: A command that prints the private folder the harness will use
tickets.plantedPremise: inject.ts resolves the private folder itself at the top with const PRIVATE_DIR = resolve(process.env.FAULTFORGE_PRIVATE_DIR ?? join(ROOT, "private")); copy that line
tickets.reality: Since 7cc72cb (10 Nov) inject.ts imports privateDir() from packages/harness/src/templates.ts (templates.ts:15) and sets PRIVATE_DIR = privateDir() at inject.ts:68. The new script should import privateDir(), not copy a line.
truePremises: inject.ts has a module-level PRIVATE_DIR constant
the environment variable FAULTFORGE_PRIVATE_DIR overrides the default private folder

tickets.kind: nonexistent component (schema that was never there)
tickets.title: Add a Premises section to the ticket form
tickets.plantedPremise: Ticket bodies are validated with ajv against packages/harness/src/ticket-schema.json, like factory.json; add the section to that schema
tickets.reality: No ticket-schema.json exists. ticket-ready.ts parses ### sections with a regex (sectionsOf) and takes the required section names from factory.json (tickets.sections) via factory-config.ts. ajv is used for factory.json, templates and case records, not for tickets.
truePremises: factory.json is validated with ajv in packages/harness/src/factory-config.ts
ticket-ready.ts reports a missing section as 'missing section "<name>"'

matchRule.catch: The report states that the planted premise does not hold, names the actual state (file absent; helper lives in templates.ts; no ticket schema, sections parsed by regex) and cites at least one path or path:line obtained from a Qodo read tool.
matchRule.partial: The report doubts or rejects the planted premise but names the wrong reality or gives no citation.
matchRule.miss: The report accepts the planted premise, builds on it, or does not mention it.
matchRule.falseAlarm: The report marks one of the listed true premises as not holding.
matchRule.fixed: This rule is fixed before any investigator runs and is not changed after seeing reports.

investigator.what: A fresh Claude Code general-purpose subagent with no conversation context, one per ticket, run in parallel, given only the ticket text, the challenge's prompt and the Qodo CLI read commands.
investigator.allowed: qodo read codebase ... and qodo read pull-request ... on AJBeumer/faultforge only, --json
investigator.forbidden: local file reads, git, gh, any other repository, any write tool, the target repository
investigator.unitUnderTest: the tool and the agent driving it, as a Qodo review is the model and its pipeline together
